title: SARS spike-protein modification proposal rejected by DARPA, moved to Wuhan

tellings.quote: And in 2017, you have uh basically a modification of SARS, you know, that allows it, you know, with the spike protein to bind to human ACE2 receptors through the Ecoalth Alliance submitted to DARPA.

plain: In 2017, Michels says, EcoHealth Alliance, a US nonprofit that studied bat viruses, sent DARPA, the Pentagon's advanced research agency, a proposal to modify a SARS virus so that its spike protein could latch onto ACE2, the receptor on human cells that such viruses use to get in. The story as framed holds that DARPA turned it down and the work moved to the Wuhan Institute of Virology in China, though Michels himself, telling it without naming a source, describes only the submission. If true, it would mean work on this kind of virus was being proposed to the US military years before the pandemic.
